observations.finding: Treated fields f_46ff and f_226 are more confluent / continuous monolayer with fewer large cell-free gaps than the DMSO control f_9fbc which shows large empty areas centrally and basally. Qualitative visual difference only - no cell count or confluence feature provided except cells_measured=542 treated; not covered by feature list.

DNA (blue) nuclei appear on average larger in area and long axis, more elliptical/irregular (less round) with increased elongation. Field f_226 shows 2-3 markedly enlarged giant nuclei (top edge, lower edge) consistent with polyploidy. DAPI appears brighter per nucleus.

Increased nuclear DNA content/size agrees with nuc_area z=3.6 (901.5 vs 792 DMSO), nuc_major_axis z=3.23 (39.2 vs 36.5), nuc_form_factor z=-5.69 (0.907 vs 0.917, less round), nuc_eccentricity z=3.58 (0.624 vs 0.601, more elliptical), nuc_dna_integrated z=4.06 (393 vs 292). Beta-tubulin (green) filament network is less distinct / less textured and more homogeneous diffuse than control where radiating microtubules are crisp and high contrast. Read from green in composite only.
Loss of texture agrees with tub_std z=-3.36 (0.077 vs 0.117) indicating reduced tubulin variance.
F-actin (red) cortical staining appears relatively more prominent vs green tubulin in treated fields; red dominates cell borders and overall field.

Increased red/green balance agrees with act_tub_ratio z=5.61 (1.284 vs 1.033). cell_nuc_area_ratio trend down z=-2.8 (3.26 vs 4.03) also consistent with larger nuclei vs cytoplasm but visual actin/tubulin ratio change is the direct match.

data.note:
Reflection note - specimen s_89e4b24a88 (chlorambucil):

**Unblinding check:** PubChem CID 2708 confirms chlorambucil (4-[4-[bis(2-chloroethyl)amino]phenyl]butanoic acid), identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree. ChEMBL CHEMBL515 annotates mechanism as DNA inhibitor (target DNA, max phase 4), consistent with BBBC021 annotation as DNA damage (alkylating nitrogen mustard).

**Phenotypic alignment:** 4 wells acquired (0.3, 1, 3, 10 µM) showed monotonic dose-dependent nuclear area increase (rho=+1.00, e10), DNA integrated intensity increase (rho+0.8, e13), cell area hypertrophy (z +11.98 at 10µM, e3) with proliferation drop (cell_count z -5.01, e3) and decreased multinucleation (e12). Microscopist at 1µM noted enlarged giant nuclei/polyploid features (e4, initially over-called Aurora), but at 10µM confirmed intact tubulin/actin networks, no bundling/depolymerization, no monopolar spindles, and decreased multinucleate fraction, ruling out microtubule/Eg5/Aurora/actin MoAs (e5). NSC vote was 4/4 DNA damage (summed similarity 1.435, e9) with k-neighbours dominated by mitomycin C, etoposide, cisplatin (e6/e9).

**Literature support:** Search for chlorambucil DNA damage alkylating mechanism returned 39 hits including Drabløs et al. DNA Repair 2004 on alkylation damage repair mechanisms and medical significance (PMID 15380096), and supporting alkylator literature (PMIDs 1352455, 23585833, 26158513). This matches the observed cytostatic hypertrophy/DNA-damage response phenotype distinct from 1-NN neighbors' mechanism but convergent on DNA damage class.

Conclusion DNA damage was correct by code scoring, supported by orthogonal dose-response, morphology negatives, and external DBO annotations.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth = chlorambucil (PubChem CID 2708, ChEMBL CHEMBL515, DNA inhibitor) = DNA damage call was correct. Assessment approved at p=0.68.

What got it right and why:

Quantitative hypertrophy + DNA content across a dosed series drove the call, not a single well. We sampled 4 doses (0.3, 1, 3, 10 µM) by acquire_well to bracket the range after list_available_experiments showing 8 doses 0.003-10 µM available. Measurements were consistent and large: e2 at 1 µM nuc_dna_integrated z=+4.1; e8 at 3 µM nuc_area z=+7.4, cell_area z=+6.2; e3 at 10 µM cell_area z=+12.0, nuc_area z=+9.9, nuc_solidity z=+6.5. Dose response over those 4 wells gave rho=+1.00 p=0 for nuc_area (e10) and rho=+0.80 p=0.2 for nuc_dna_integrated (e13) with falling cell_count rho=-0.80 (e11, e7 z=-2.2 at 0.3 µM already) - classic proliferation inhibition with G1/S or G2/M arrest-related enlargement. No new assay invented this; the orthogonal test proposed was γH2AX/p53/p21 + FACS but not run in this screen.

Comparison to reference atlas was decisive and stable. e6 NSC 2/2 DNA damage, 6/10 neighbours DNA damage/Aurora 3/10/replication 1/10 expanded to e9 NSC 4/4 DNA damage, 7/10 neighbours DNA damage after we added 0.3 and 3 µM. That consistency across 4 independent acquisitions outweighed single-microscopist variance.

Critical discriminator was multinucleation. Aurora, Eg5 and microtubule classes predict increased multinucleation/monopolar spindles/bundling. We specifically acquired dose_response for frac_multinucleate_proxy: rho=-0.80 (e12), z strongly negative at 10 µM, and describe_phenotype on 4 fields at high dose (e5) explicitly reported 10 observations with lower density vs DMSO, intact tubulin/actin, and ruled out microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers, actin disruptors, Aurora, Eg5. That e5 read directly contradicted the earlier 2-field 1 µM read (e4) that had suggested Aurora/DNA replication/DNA damage with 7 observations and paradoxically higher density vs DMSO, plus outlier cytoskeletal signal act_tub_ratio z=+5.6 and nuc_form_factor z=-5.7 in e2. We correctly down-weighted e4/e2 as noisy low-dose shape irregularity and kept DNA damage 0.70 vs replication 0.15 vs Aurora 0.08 in update_hypotheses (e14).

What misled / limitations:

1. e4 vs e5 density contradiction: higher vs DMSO at 1 µM then lower vs DMSO at 10 µM. Without the 0.3-10 µM dose responses we would have over-called Aurora on e2 form factor alone. Bridging acquisition at 3 µM (e8) showed monotonic hypertrophy that resolved it.
2. Statistical power: with only 4 wells, cell_count and DNA-integrated and multinucleate rho values were directionally correct but p=0.2 (e11-e13), not significant. The review correctly notes all wells were single-replicate; large effect sizes (+12.0, +9.9) mitigated but replicates would be needed. The submitted 0.68 was well calibrated for residual DNA replication ambiguity - atlas cannot separate DNA damage from DNA replication on morphology alone, needs orthogonal damage-response assay.
3. Literature gap in-run: PubMed search for 'DNA damage nuclear enlargement cell area increase cell cycle arrest phenotype' returned 0 hits (e19), so that phenotype inference was made without direct citation. Chlorambucil alkylating-agent mechanism itself is supported in returned literature on alkylation damage in DNA and alkylating agents inducing DNA damage and checkpoint activation PMID 15380096, PMID 26158513, PMID 23585833, without needing to invent a chlorambucil-specific cytology paper.

Unblinding (e16/e17) confirms name and BBBC021 structure agree for chlorambucil DNA inhibitor, consistent with DNA damage. No clinical implications inferred; this is screening morphology only. Next step if real lab remains as proposed: γH2AX foci + p53/p21 and cell-cycle arrest profiling vs a reference DNA damage control and an Aurora inhibitor to test divergence on multinucleation.

The submitted 0.68 was well calibrated for residual DNA replication ambiguity - atlas cannot separate DNA damage from DNA replication on morphology alone, needs orthogonal damage-response assay.
3. Literature gap in-run: PubMed search for 'DNA damage nuclear enlargement cell area increase cell cycle arrest phenotype' returned 0 hits (e19), so that phenotype inference was made without direct citation. Chlorambucil alkylating-agent mechanism itself is supported in returned literature on alkylation damage in DNA and alkylating agents inducing DNA damage and checkpoint activation PMID 15380096, PMID 26158513, PMID 23585833, without needing to invent a chlorambucil-specific cytology paper.

Unblinding (e16/e17) confirms name and BBBC021 structure agree for chlorambucil DNA inhibitor, consistent with DNA damage. No clinical implications inferred; this is screening morphology only. Next step if real lab remains as proposed: γH2AX foci + p53/p21 and cell-cycle arrest profiling vs a reference DNA damage control and an Aurora inhibitor to test divergence on multinucleation.
